questions.q: Which table stores every email notification record in a ServiceNow instance?
options: sysevent_email_action
sysevent_email_template
sysevent_in_email_action
sys_user_group
questions.explain: System Notification > Email > Notifications lists rows on sysevent_email_action — that's the notification record itself.

questions.q: A notification is set to fire when Incident's State field changes to Resolved. What kind of trigger is this?
options: A named event fired by gs.eventQueue()
A record condition trigger scoped to a specific field change
An inbound email action
An email template placeholder
questions.explain: Tying the trigger directly to a field changing on a table record is the record condition trigger — the most common mechanism.

questions.q: What mechanism lets a Business Rule or Flow Designer action fire a notification for something too complex to express as a simple field condition, like an SLA breach calculation?
options: Queuing a named event with gs.eventQueue(), which a notification can listen for by event name
Editing the sysevent_email_template table directly
Adding the condition to an Inbound Email Action instead
There is no way to trigger a notification from a script
questions.explain: A script can queue a named event into sysevent; a notification configured with that event name as its trigger fires independently of any direct record condition.

questions.q: A notification's recipient is set to "Assigned to," but the goal was to notify the caller when their incident resolves. What's wrong?
options: The trigger condition is checking the wrong table
The Who will receive it configuration points at the wrong field, so the assignee gets the email instead of the caller
sysevent_email_action doesn't support per-record recipients
Email Templates cannot reference the caller field
questions.explain: Trigger and recipients are configured independently — a correct trigger with the wrong recipient field still sends the email to the wrong person.

questions.q: Why would an administrator add additional filter conditions (e.g., Priority is 1 - Critical) on top of a notification's basic State-change trigger?
options: To change which table the notification is attached to
To convert the trigger from a record condition into an event trigger
To scope the notification to only the subset of resolutions that genuinely warrant that email to that audience, rather than covering every resolution
Additional filter conditions are not supported on notification records
questions.explain: Stacking narrow, clearly-scoped notifications is better administration than one broad notification with conditions nobody can reason about later.
